tests.ShortDescription: Opening an existing order on the Sales Orders form (SO301000) with Acumatica's real sales-order logic and reading what the form shows: header, lines, taxes, shipments, payments, addresses, contacts, currency, commissions and discounts.
tests.Question: How fast does a sales order open on screen?
tests.WhatItSimulates: Opening an existing order on the Sales Orders form (SO301000) with Acumatica's real sales-order logic and reading what the form shows: header, lines, taxes, shipments, payments, addresses, contacts, currency, commissions and discounts.
tests.WhyItMatters: Opening a document is what everyone does all day. It is not one big query but 15-25 small ones, so the fixed cost of each request to the database matters more than raw power. This number is the database-dependent part of opening the form; the browser and the network add the same time on every database.

tests.DisplayName: Find a customer by part of the name
tests.ShortDescription: The quick search in the customer selector: a 'contains' search on customer ID and name, all matches returned.
tests.Question: When I type part of a customer's name, how fast do matches appear, and does every database find the same customers?
tests.WhatItSimulates: The quick search in the customer selector: a 'contains' search on customer ID and name, all matches returned.
tests.WhyItMatters: The customer list is small, so speed differences here mostly reflect the fixed cost of each request to the database. The bigger message is about answers: a wildcard search cannot use a normal index on any of these databases, and the three treat accented letters differently. If your names contain accents, users can see different search results depending on the database.

tests.ShortDescription: The trial balance / account summary logic: for every branch, account and subaccount, take the latest general-ledger balance at or before the chosen period, using Acumatica's own GLHistoryByPeriod view.
tests.Question: How long does a month-end trial balance take?
tests.WhatItSimulates: The trial balance / account summary logic: for every branch, account and subaccount, take the latest general-ledger balance at or before the chosen period, using Acumatica's own GLHistoryByPeriod view.
tests.WhyItMatters: Month-end close runs many balance reports like this. For every account it must find the latest balance at or before the chosen month, a demanding kind of question that databases can handle in very different ways. If finance runs many balance reports at close, watch this test.

tests.ShortDescription: A clerk entering an order on the Sales Orders form with the full business logic: defaults, pricing, availability, the inventory plan, numbering and save — about 20-40 database statements across about ten tables in one transaction.
tests.Question: How long does saving a typical 3-line sales order take?
tests.WhatItSimulates: A clerk entering an order on the Sales Orders form with the full business logic: defaults, pricing, availability, the inventory plan, numbering and save — about 20-40 database statements across about ten tables in one transaction.
tests.WhyItMatters: This is the everyday write that order desks and integrations do thousands of times a day. One person's save time is mostly Acumatica's own work; any remaining gap between databases is the cost of many small reads and writes inside one business transaction plus how fast each database commits.

tests.DisplayName: Enter sales orders – 4 clerks working non-stop
tests.ShortDescription: A busy order desk: 4, 8 or 16 clerks each entering orders non-stop, with no pause between orders, for different customers and products. The only shared rows are the order-number counter and system bookkeeping.
tests.Question: When more people enter orders at the same time, how many orders per minute does the system handle, and how much longer does each person wait?
tests.WhatItSimulates: A busy order desk: 4, 8 or 16 clerks each entering orders non-stop, with no pause between orders, for different customers and products. The only shared rows are the order-number counter and system bookkeeping.
tests.WhyItMatters: This is the scaling question that matters most for a growing company. A database that handles parallel work well keeps raising orders per minute from 1 to 16 clerks with only a modest rise in each clerk's wait. Because nobody pauses, 16 clerks here stand for a much larger real team.

tests.DisplayName: Everyone sells the best-seller – 16 clerks working non-stop
tests.ShortDescription: The same busy order desk, but every order includes the best-selling item from the same warehouse, so every save must update the same stock-availability row and saves queue behind each other.
tests.Question: What happens when everyone sells the same popular product at the same moment?
tests.WhatItSimulates: The same busy order desk, but every order includes the best-selling item from the same warehouse, so every save must update the same stock-availability row and saves queue behind each other.
tests.WhyItMatters: Real businesses have hot spots: one bestseller, one warehouse, one GL account. Compare with the spread version at the same number of people: it shows whether each database's locking makes people wait in an orderly line, hit deadlocks that Acumatica must retry, or fail outright.

tests.DisplayName: Create and release invoices to the GL – 1 person
tests.ShortDescription: Invoices and Memos (AR301000) followed by Release with automatic GL posting: the invoice, customer balance, AR history, a new GL batch and the GL balances for this period and all later periods are written.
tests.Question: How long does it take to create a customer invoice, release it and post it to the general ledger?
tests.WhatItSimulates: Invoices and Memos (AR301000) followed by Release with automatic GL posting: the invoice, customer balance, AR history, a new GL batch and the GL balances for this period and all later periods are written.
tests.WhyItMatters: Releasing and posting documents is the heaviest routine write in accounting. Each release updates running totals that many documents share. The 1-person number shows the raw cost of posting; if month-end close is your bottleneck, weight this family most.

tests.DisplayName: Create and release invoices to the GL – 4 people working non-stop
tests.ShortDescription: Four people releasing invoices for different customers at once; all post to the same AR and sales accounts, so they share the same GL balance rows — the real contention of a month-end mass release.
tests.Question: Can four people release and post invoices at the same time, or do they queue?
tests.WhatItSimulates: Four people releasing invoices for different customers at once; all post to the same AR and sales accounts, so they share the same GL balance rows — the real contention of a month-end mass release.
tests.WhyItMatters: Month-end batches are often released side by side. This shows whether posting scales with more people or turns into a queue, and whether any database has to retry or fails.

tests.ShortDescription: The import and API create path without business logic: records go through Acumatica's cache with audit fields and are committed 250 at a time.
tests.Question: How quickly can Acumatica save brand-new records (imports, integrations, bulk entry)?
tests.WhatItSimulates: The import and API create path without business logic: records go through Acumatica's cache with audit fields and are committed 250 at a time.
tests.WhyItMatters: Imports, integrations and nightly syncs are mostly 'save many new records'. The 1-worker/8-worker pair also shows whether a database lets several writers work at once or makes them queue, which matters if you run heavy integrations next to interactive users.

tests.DisplayName: Stock availability list, only the needed columns – 1 worker
tests.ShortDescription: The same availability list read through a 10-column projection (Acumatica's tool for lists that fetch only the columns they show).
tests.Question: How much faster is the same list when only the needed columns are fetched?
tests.WhatItSimulates: The same availability list read through a 10-column projection (Acumatica's tool for lists that fetch only the columns they show).
tests.WhyItMatters: It shows whether a database's advantage survives when the application asks for less data. If the gap shrinks a lot here, the difference was in moving wide rows, not in the database's query engine.
